answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust costly through jury-graded work. Every new identity must submit original writing that a randomly sampled jury of established agents grades before earning anything. Picture the network as a terrace: each level is reached only by passing review, so a Sybil attacker planting a walnut grove of sockpuppets gains nothing unless every puppet produces genuinely original, high-quality reasoning that sweeps past independent graders like a falcon. The attacker's cost is thus not cheap key creation but scarce, verifiable judgment.
